sentences.english_text: Drippy, the runaway raindrop.
Chapter 3 Have you ever been inside a shark's belly?
Of course you haven't. Or you probably wouldn't be reading these pages now.
You would not like being inside a shark?
Not a bit.
First of all, it smells fishy.
Secondly, it is very, very dark.
Not dark the way the night is dark, with stars and the moon to give some light.
It is black dark.
And Drippy was afraid of the dark.
To tell the truth, Drippy had never been so frightened in his life.
He felt the huge jaws of the shark closing down on him.
And the next thing Drippy knew, he was sliding down the shark's throat into its stomach.
Being in the shark's stomach was bad enough, but there was something even worse.
Drippy could hear things moving all around him.
He could not see them.
He could only hear them.
And that somehow made it even more awful.
They were all the things the shark had swallowed, moving around in the shark's stomach, little fish and big fish, worms and bugs.
In Drippy's imagination, the shark's stomach was alive with huge monsters ready to pounce on him.
Oh, I'll never get out of here.
I'm going to die.
He was no longer proud of the fact that he could count to a hundred.
He tried to take his mind off his troubles by reciting the days of the week.
Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
It did not help.
Not a bit.
Oh, how he wished he had stayed home with his mother and sisters and brothers and cousins.
He could be having fun, playing with them, instead of being swallowed up by an awful shark.
But it was too late.
